newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
SYDNEY HARBOUR IN OLYMPIC MODE
Sydney Harbour will swing into an Olympic mode this weekend as many present and potential Olympic sailors begin their long haul towards Sydney 2000.

More than 200 sailors from all parts of Australia and overseas will be contesting the Yachting Association of New South Wales' Sail Sydney '97 Easter Regatta in seven of the ten Olympics classes for 2000. With travel grants available from the NSW Yachting Foundation for successful competitors, Sail Sydney is an important step towards international campaigns for the younger potential Olympians.

Three major clubs are involved in conducting the regatta for the Yachting Association -- Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron, Middle Harbour Yacht Club and Woollahra Sailing Club -- with the event also an important training regatta in race management for the Olympics.

Sail Sydney 97 is the first of three Olympic classes regattas on the Harbour this year with international competitors already wanting to experience sailing conditions, particularly in late September, when the Olympic Regatta will be held in 2000.

Sail Sydney 97 will see the debut of Star class bronze medallist COLIN BEASHEL in the Soling class, now the only Olympic keelboat class, but already up against keen competition from other Olympic aspirants GARY GIETZ and NEVILLE WITTEY.

WITTEY is in top form, having just successfully defended the Sayonara Cup match-race challenge for Royal Prince Edward Yacht Club sailing Dragon class keelboats and completing an outstanding season in the Etchells class.

Of major interest will be the debut of World 18-footer champion CHRIS NICHOLSON in the new Olympic class, the Australian-designed 49-er skiff, while another competitor will NICOLA BETHWAITE, sister of the designer of the 49-er, JULIAN BETHWAITE. Nicola is a former Olympian in the 470 women's dinghy class and a world champion in Cherubs.

The biggest fleet will be in the Laser class, with Olympian MICHAEL BOOTH and ANDREW LANDENBERGER who have split after winning the silver medal at Savannah, BOOTH now sailing with ADAM BEASHEL as crew while Landenberger has PETER THORPE as his crew.
THE MIGHTY AMAZON FLOWS ON

One of the great ocean races on the Australian calendar is the Sydney to Mooloolaba race conducted each year (this year was the 25th) by Middle Harbour Yacht Club in association with the gregarious Mooloolaba Yacht Club on Queensland's Sunshine Coast.

After a light start, the breeze kicked in, giving most of the fleet a rollicking ride north under spinnakers on the final day and giving Cruising Yacht Club of Australia's PETER WALKER his fourth line honours victory in the 470 nautical mile autumn ocean classic.

In a race that saw the lead change many times, Amaxon regained the lead in the final 28 miles across Moreton Bay to win by less than four minutes after a great duel with Exile, the "lean mean green machine," skippered by WARWICK MILLER, the Hong Kong watch-making entrepreneur.

On handicap, BZW Challenge, the US-built Corel 45 imported by Sydney based and successful international ocean racing yachtsman RAY ROBERTSON won the top-of-the line IMS Racer Division One, beating successful international campaigners such as SYD FISCHER's Ragamuffin, ANDREW STRACHAN's Ninety Seven and Warwick Miller's Exile.

Atara's third in the IMS Racer Division Two was sufficient to give skipper and CYCA director ROGER HICKSMAN and the Lyons 43 his first ever IMS Blue Water Point Score, the prestigious series of ocean races run by the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia but contested by all Sydney clubs. This division saw a fine win by Quest, the Nelson/Marek 43 owned by travelman BOB STEEL.

Queensland kept in the winner's circle with No Fearr, the successful Far 39 owned and skippered by young Townsville yachtsman CAREY RAMM, surviving a protest to win the strong IMS Cruiser/Racer Division and will continue her voyage north in home waters with the owner's sights on more victories.

The Race Committee found that RAMM had breached the sailing instructions for the Mooloolaba race by carrying an advertising logo - in this case Super League - on the mainsail of No Fearr when the rules limited advertising to spinnakers only. However, they used their prerogative and issued only a warning.
The decision opens up a can of worms in the rules governing advertising and although the international rules seem explicit there are obviously areas which need clarification.

Since being launched late last year the Farr 39 has won the Hayman Island Big Boat Series and Hamilton Island Race Week in Queensland, the Bruce & Walsh and Telstra Cup regattas in Sydney, finished second in its division of the Telstra Sydney to Hobart and has now won IMS/Cruiser/Racer division of the 34th Sydney to Mooloolaba race.
AUSSIE CUP CREW CLOSE CECOND IN NEW ZEALAND

The Australian Admirals Cup crew led by GRANT SIMMER and Colin Beashel has finished a close second in the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron's International Regatta in Auckland, sailing the ILC40, G'Net, which they have chartered for the Admirals Cup in England later in the year.

The Australians had a slight edge on the local oppositions throughout the regatta and going into the last of 11 races, a 160 nautical mile coastal race of the hard-fought regatta, the G'net had a half point lead from the Neq Zealand sloop Georgia, helmed by DAVID BARNES with ROD DAVIS as tactician.

However, Georgia staked her claim right from the start, holding a varying lead around the course out in the Hauraki Gulf. As they worked back into Auckland Harbour last Saturday morning, Georgia was just two minutes in front but it was sufficient to give the NZ yacht a comfortable handicap win in the double points race and overall honours by a slender 1.5 points.

In the Mumm 30 division, Middle Harbour Yacht Club member and director of Corinthian Doors, RICHARD PIRINI finished equal first with New Zealander JOHN ST CLAIR BROWN but lost on a countback. ST CLAIR BROWN won six of the 11 races, PIRINI five in some heavy air sailing, skippering a brand new Mumm 30 appropriately named Corinthian Doors.
WITTEY RETAINS SAYONARA CUP

Back on Sydney Harbour, NEVILLE WITTEY and his crew DAVID GILES and MIKE TYQUIN have successfully defended the historic Sayonara Cup on behalf of the Royal Prince Edward Yacht Club, that tiny club that nestles among the foreshore mansions of Point Piper.

According to fellow yachting scribe BOB ROSS (himself a member of "The Edwards") WITTEY showed "brutal aggression on the starting lines" to demolish the Royal Yacht Club of Tasmania's DAVID GRANEY and his crew in four straight match races.

WITTEY last season won the Tasmanians, the 93-year-old trophy for interstate competition between clubs, sailed on America's Cup match racing rules, but now in Dragon class one-design yachts. Word is that the RYCT will challenge again next year.
* Peter Campbell is editor of OFFSHORE Yachting magazine.
